svg.data-vd-steps: [[0, "The human skeleton: over 200 bones. Its functions: support, protection, movement, making blood cells and storing minerals."], [1, "Protection: the skull protects the brain, the rib cage the heart and lungs, and the vertebrae the spinal cord."], [4.5, "Movement: muscles pull on bones at joints. The elbow is a hinge joint: the forearm bends up and down."], [8, "Making blood cells: red bone marrow in bones such as the femur, sternum and pelvis makes red and white blood cells."], [11, "Support: the skeleton holds the body up and gives it shape. Bones also store calcium and phosphate."]]
svg.title: The human skeleton
svg.desc: Front view of the human skeleton with the skull, vertebral column, ribs, clavicle, humerus, radius and ulna, hand bones, pelvis, femur, patella, tibia and fibula, and foot bones, with a tour of its functions.
svg.text: Simplified: not every bone is drawn.

g.data-info: Protects the brain. The jaw (mandible) is the only bone of the skull that moves.
A chain of vertebrae: supports the body, allows bending, protects the spinal cord.
The rib cage protects the heart and lungs and moves during breathing.
Connects the arm to the body.
Supports the weight of the upper body; protects organs in the abdomen; ball-and-socket hip joints.
Upper arm bone. Joined to the radius and ulna at the elbow (a hinge joint).
Many small bones in the wrist and hand allow precise movement.
Thigh bone: the longest and strongest bone. Its red bone marrow makes blood cells.
Bones of the ankle and foot.

g.text: red bone marrow makes blood cells
